stem: To draw the graph of \(4x + 5y = 19\), find \(y\) when \(x = 1\):
solution: Put \(x = 1\): \(4(1) + 5y = 19 \Rightarrow 5y = 15 \Rightarrow y = 3\).

stem: Out of the following equations which one is NOT a quadratic equation?
solution: In option A, \(x^2 + 4x = 11 + x^2 \Rightarrow 4x = 11\), a linear equation (the \(x^2\) terms cancel), so it is NOT quadratic. Options B, C and D all retain an \(x^2\) term and are quadratic.

stem: For the given A.P., \(a = 3.5\), \(d = 0\), then \(t_n =\) ______

solution: \(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{2}{n(S)} \Rightarrow n(S) = 2 \times 5 = 10\).

Find the common difference of the following A.P.: \(2, 4, 6, 8, \ldots\)
solution: The common difference \(d = t_2 - t_1 = 4 - 2 = 2\).

stem: On a certain article if the rate of CGST is 9%, then what is the rate of SGST?
solution: For any intra-state supply, CGST and SGST are always equal. \(\therefore\) the rate of SGST is also 9%.

stem: If one coin is tossed, write the sample space \(S\).
solution: When one coin is tossed the possible outcomes are Head and Tail, so \(S = \{H, T\}\) and \(n(S) = 2\).

stem:
Complete the following activity to find the value of \(x\):
\(5x + 3y = 9\) ...... (I)
\(2x - 3y = 12\) ...... (II)
Add equations (I) and (II) and hence find \(x\).
solution: Adding (I) and (II): \((5x + 3y) + (2x - 3y) = 9 + 12 \Rightarrow 7x = 21 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{21}{7} = 3\).

stem: Complete the following activity to determine the nature of the roots of the quadratic equation \(x^2 + 2x - 9 = 0\).
solution:
Compare \(x^2 + 2x - 9 = 0\) with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\): \(a = 1\), \(b = 2\), \(c = -9\).
\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (2)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times (-9) = 4 + 36 = 40\).
Since \(\Delta = 40 > 0\), the roots of the equation are real and unequal.

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem:
Complete the following table using the given information:

| Sr. No. | FV | Share is at | MV |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ₹100 | Par | ? |
| 2 | ? | Premium ₹500 | ₹575 |
| 3 | ₹10 | ? | ₹5 |
| 4 | ₹200 | Discount ₹50 | ? |
solution:
Using MV = FV + Premium (at premium), MV = FV − Discount (at discount), and MV = FV (at par):

| Sr. No. | FV | Share is at | MV |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ₹100 | Par | ₹100 |
| 2 | ₹75 | Premium ₹500 | ₹575 |
| 3 | ₹10 | Discount ₹5 | ₹5 |
| 4 | ₹200 | Discount ₹50 | ₹150 |

Row 1: at par MV \(=\) FV \(=\) ₹100. Row 2: FV \(=\) MV \(-\) Premium \(= 575 - 500 =\) ₹75. Row 3: MV \(<\) FV, so the share is at Discount \(=\) FV \(-\) MV \(= 10 - 5 =\) ₹5. Row 4: MV \(=\) FV \(-\) Discount \(= 200 - 50 =\) ₹150.

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations: \(x + y = 4\); \(2x - y = 2\).
solution: Add the two equations: \((x + y) + (2x - y) = 4 + 2 \Rightarrow 3x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 2\). Substitute in \(x + y = 4\): \(2 + y = 4 \Rightarrow y = 2\). \(\therefore x = 2, y = 2\).

stem: Write the following equation in the form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), then write the values of \(a\), \(b\), \(c\): \(2y = 10 - y^2\).
Write an A.P. whose first term is \(a = 10\) and common difference \(d = 5\).
solution: The terms are \(a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, \ldots\) i.e. \(10, 15, 20, 25, \ldots\)

stem: A courier service agent charged a total of ₹590 to courier a parcel from Nashik to Nagpur. In the tax invoice the taxable value is ₹500, on which CGST is ₹45 and SGST is ₹45. Find the rate of GST charged for this service.
solution: Total GST \(=\) CGST \(+\) SGST \(= 45 + 45 =\) ₹90 on a taxable value of ₹500. Rate of GST \(= \dfrac{90}{500} \times 100 = 18\%\).

stem:
Form a 'Road Safety Committee' of two, from 2 boys \(B_1, B_2\) and 2 girls \(G_1, G_2\). Complete the following activity to write the sample space:
(a) Committee of 2 boys
(b) Committee of 2 girls
(c) Committee of one boy and one girl
(d) Sample space \(S\)
solution:
(a) Committee of 2 boys \(= \{B_1 B_2\}\).
(b) Committee of 2 girls \(= \{G_1 G_2\}\).
(c) Committee of one boy and one girl \(= \{B_1 G_1, B_1 G_2, B_2 G_1, B_2 G_2\}\).
(d) Sample space \(S = \{B_1 B_2,\ B_1 G_1,\ B_2 G_1,\ B_1 G_2,\ B_2 G_2,\ G_1 G_2\}\), so \(n(S) = 6\).

Solve the following simultaneous equations using Cramer's rule: \(4m + 6n = 54\); \(3m + 2n = 28\).
solution:
\(D = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 8 - 18 = -10\).
\(D_m = \begin{vmatrix} 54 & 6 \\ 28 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 108 - 168 = -60\).
\(D_n = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 54 \\ 3 & 28 \end{vmatrix} = 112 - 162 = -50\).
\(m = \dfrac{D_m}{D} = \dfrac{-60}{-10} = 6\), \(n = \dfrac{D_n}{D} = \dfrac{-50}{-10} = 5\). \(\therefore m = 6, n = 5\).

subtopic: Solving by Formula and Completing the Square
stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by the formula method: \(x^2 + 10x + 2 = 0\).

A two digit number is formed with the digits 2, 3, 5, 7, 9 without repetition. What is the probability of the following events?
Event A: The number formed is an odd number.
Event B: The number formed is a multiple of 5.
solution:
Total two-digit numbers \(= 5 \times 4 = 20\), so \(n(S) = 20\).
Event A (odd): the units digit must be odd, i.e. one of \(3, 5, 7, 9\) (4 choices), and the tens digit is any of the remaining 4 digits: \(n(A) = 4 \times 4 = 16\). \(P(A) = \dfrac{16}{20} = \dfrac{4}{5}\).
Event B (multiple of 5): the units digit must be 5 (1 choice), tens digit any of the remaining 4 digits: \(n(B) = 4\). \(P(B) = \dfrac{4}{20} = \dfrac{1}{5}\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
The frequency distribution table shows the number of mango trees in a grove and their yield of mangoes. Find the median of the data:

| No. of Mangoes | No. of Trees |
|---|---|
| 50–100 | 33 |
| 100–150 | 30 |
| 150–200 | 90 |
| 200–250 | 80 |
| 250–300 | 17 |
solution:
Cumulative frequencies: 33, 63, 153, 233, 250. Here \(N = 250\), so \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 125\), which lies in the class 150–200 (median class).
\(L = 150\), cf \(= 63\), \(f = 90\), \(h = 50\).
Median \(= L + \left(\dfrac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f}\right) \times h = 150 + \left(\dfrac{125 - 63}{90}\right) \times 50 = 150 + \dfrac{62 \times 50}{90} = 150 + 34.44 = 184.44\) (approx).

subtopic: Sum of n Terms of an A.P.
stem: If the first term of an A.P. is \(p\), the second term is \(q\) and the last term is \(r\), then show that the sum of all the terms is \((q + r - 2p) \times \dfrac{(p + r)}{2(q - p)}\).
solution:
The common difference \(d = q - p\). Let there be \(n\) terms with last term \(r\).
\(r = p + (n - 1)d \Rightarrow n - 1 = \dfrac{r - p}{q - p} \Rightarrow n = \dfrac{r - p}{q - p} + 1 = \dfrac{r - p + q - p}{q - p} = \dfrac{q + r - 2p}{q - p}\).
Sum \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(\text{first term} + \text{last term}) = \dfrac{n}{2}(p + r) = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{q + r - 2p}{q - p} \cdot (p + r) = (q + r - 2p) \times \dfrac{(p + r)}{2(q - p)}\). Hence proved.

stem: The sum of the squares of five consecutive natural numbers is 1455. Find the numbers.
solution:
Let the five consecutive natural numbers be \(n-2, n-1, n, n+1, n+2\).
Sum of squares \(= (n-2)^2 + (n-1)^2 + n^2 + (n+1)^2 + (n+2)^2 = 5n^2 + 10 = 1455\).
\(5n^2 = 1445 \Rightarrow n^2 = 289 \Rightarrow n = 17\) (natural number).
\(\therefore\) the numbers are \(15, 16, 17, 18, 19\). (Check: \(225 + 256 + 289 + 324 + 361 = 1455\).)

stem: Draw the graph of the equation \(x + 2y = 4\). Find the area of the triangle formed by the line intersecting the X-axis and the Y-axis.
solution:
For the X-intercept put \(y = 0\): \(x = 4\), giving the point \((4, 0)\). For the Y-intercept put \(x = 0\): \(2y = 4 \Rightarrow y = 2\), giving the point \((0, 2)\). The line meets the axes at \(A(4, 0)\) and \(B(0, 2)\); with the origin \(O(0, 0)\) they form a right triangle.
Area \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 2 = 4\) square units.

stem: A survey was conducted for 180 people in a city. 70 ate pizza, 60 ate burgers and 50 ate chips. Draw a pie diagram for the given information.
solution:
Total people \(= 70 + 60 + 50 = 180\). The central angle for each item \(= \dfrac{\text{value}}{180} \times 360^\circ\).
Pizza: \(\dfrac{70}{180} \times 360^\circ = 140^\circ\).
Burgers: \(\dfrac{60}{180} \times 360^\circ = 120^\circ\).
Chips: \(\dfrac{50}{180} \times 360^\circ = 100^\circ\).
(Total \(= 140^\circ + 120^\circ + 100^\circ = 360^\circ\).) Draw a circle and mark three sectors with these central angles to obtain the required pie diagram.
